<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is standard packaging for a Node.js-based application from its own upstream GitHub repository.

- The `source` array downloads a tarball from `https://github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec/archive/v${pkgver}.tar.gz`, which is the project's own upstream. This is expected and normal.
- The `sha256sums` array contains a proper, pinned SHA256 checksum (`debe56f5...`), so the downloaded archive is verified.
- There is no `pkgver()` function, so no VCS probing executes at source time.
- The top-level/global scope contains no command substitution, no `eval`, no `curl`/`wget` calls, no obfuscated or encoded strings, and no exfiltration logic. Only standard variable assignments and array definitions.
- `prepare()`, `build()`, and `package()` will not run under `--nobuild --noprepare`, so the esbuild postinstall allowance and pnpm install in `prepare()` are out of scope for this gate.

No malicious behavior triggers during sourcing or source-fetching.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Standard PKGBUILD with pinned source and checksum; no malicious top-level code.</summary>
</security_assessment>
